subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: What session-health breaker contract should OpenClaw core own before implementation: a unified receipt/state model, a narrow no-progress counter, or deferral to narrower guard issues?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior crosses failure taxonomy, config defaults, persisted session state, recovery actions, UI/operator surfacing, and overlap with existing retry policy, so code alone cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design unified session-health receipts
options.body: Define failure signatures, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, cooldown or half-open behavior, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

options.title: Land a narrow no-progress breaker
options.body: Limit the first change to a bounded consecutive no-progress counter in the embedded run loop while leaving UI receipts, persistence, cooldowns, and auto-rotation as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, tool-loop, compaction, provider, cron, and subagent guard tracks separate and close or narrow this umbrella later.

recommendation.title: Design unified session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Define failure signatures, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, cooldown or half-open behavior, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest adjacent history is the merged idle-timeout breaker and retry/loop policy work, making this the best available routing candidate for the product contract choice.
